esnName.label: What is your company or activity called?
esnName.subtitle: Trading name (not the registered legal name)

consultantSize.label: How many consultants does your organisation have?

consultantCount.label: And the exact number, if you know it?
consultantCount.subtitle: Refines the range above — leave blank if you don't have it handy

esnWebsite.label: What is your website, if you have one?
esnWebsite.subtitle: Leave blank if it doesn't have one — never blocking

annualRevenueAmount.label: What's your company's annual revenue?
annualRevenueAmount.subtitle: Optional — leave blank if you'd rather not share it

annualRevenuePeriod.label: Which period does this figure cover?
annualRevenuePeriod.subtitle: Revenue without a period doesn't mean much — the last closed fiscal year isn't the current one

salesTeamSize.label: How many people take part in business development?
salesTeamSize.subtitle: Separate from company size — a 200-person company might have just 2 salespeople

esnMaturitySituation.label: Where is your business right now?
esnMaturitySituation.subtitle: This changes what we offer you — a company just starting out doesn't get the same audit as a growing one

esnMaturitySituationChoices.transformationExample: E.g.: moving from solo freelancing to a structured company, or changing your business model
esnMaturitySituationChoices.buExample: BU = Business Unit, a subsidiary or agency with its own activity

companyGrowthGoal.label: What's the company's goal right now?

activeClientsBand.label: How many active clients right now?

revenueRecurrence.label: Is your revenue mostly recurring or one-off?

clientConcentrationRisk.label: Does one client weigh heavily in your revenue?

consultantsManagedByUserBand.label: How many consultants do you manage directly?
consultantsManagedByUserBand.subtitle: Separate from the company's total size

availableConsultantsBand.label: How many consultants are available right now (bench)?

consultantSizeGroupBand.label: And across the whole group, if you're part of one?
consultantSizeGroupBand.subtitle: Leave blank if your company isn't part of a group - not the same count as the question above

consultantSizeBusinessUnitBand.label: And in your BU / agency specifically, if you have one?
consultantSizeBusinessUnitBand.subtitle: Leave blank if you don't have a separate BU - a figure scoped to you, not the whole group

talentPoolIdentifiedBand.label: How many profiles are identified in your pool (CV received, contact made)?
talentPoolIdentifiedBand.subtitle: A rough band is enough

talentPoolQualifiedBand.label: How many of them are qualified (file checked)?

talentPoolAvailableBand.label: How many are available right now?
talentPoolAvailableBand.subtitle: Distinct from the bench band you declared above

talentPoolAvailabilityRecencyBand.label: When did you last check that availability?
talentPoolAvailabilityRecencyBand.subtitle: A recency band, not an exact date

talentPoolAvgTjmBand.label: What's your pool's average day rate?
talentPoolAvgTjmBand.subtitle: Your pool's rate, not the one you sell

talentPoolConsentStatus.label: Which framework allows your talent pool profiles to be used and shared?
talentPoolConsentStatus.subtitle: One overall answer, not per record

talentPoolOtherProcessesBand.label: How many of these profiles are also in process elsewhere?

talentPoolEngagementRealityBand.label: How many would truly be available right away?

talentPoolRevalidationFrequency.label: How often do you revalidate these availabilities?

talentPoolStateInterestedBand.label: How many profiles are at the "interested" stage?
talentPoolStateInterestedBand.subtitle: A CV and a declared availability somewhere, not yet qualified

talentPoolStateAvailableBand.label: How many are at the "available" stage?
talentPoolStateAvailableBand.subtitle: Qualified AND available in the short term

talentPoolStateSecuredBand.label: How many are at the "secured" stage?
talentPoolStateSecuredBand.subtitle: Commitment confirmed in writing

talentPoolStatePresentableBand.label: How many are at the "presentable" stage?
talentPoolStatePresentableBand.subtitle: The file is ready to send to a client — a CV is not a ready application

clientBaseMissionsOngoingBand.label: How many missions are currently ongoing?

clientBaseMissionsCompletedBand.label: How many missions ended in the last 12 months?

clientBaseSatisfactionBand.label: Is your clients' satisfaction tracked?
clientBaseSatisfactionBand.subtitle: This is about tracking, not the score itself

clientBaseReferralsBand.label: Do you get referrals from current clients?

clientBaseRexBand.label: Do you run a debrief after each mission?
clientBaseRexBand.subtitle: What worked, what got stuck

clientBaseCaseStudiesBand.label: How many client case studies are usable today?
clientBaseCaseStudiesBand.subtitle: Ready to show a prospect, not just remembered

clientBaseCrossSellBand.label: Have you already offered a complementary service to an existing client?

clientBaseDeadlinesBand.label: Are your missions' deadlines tracked 3 months out?
clientBaseDeadlinesBand.subtitle: An estimate is enough — no need for an exhaustive inventory.

clientBaseFollowupRegularity.label: Is the follow-up on your client accounts regular?

clientBaseFollowupOwner.label: Who is responsible for this follow-up?
clientBaseFollowupOwner.subtitle: A role or a first name, whatever fits

expertiseAreas.label: What are your areas of expertise?
expertiseAreas.subtitle: Several choices allowed — keep the ones you really deliver

positioningChoices.niche: You are known for one or two very specific subjects, where few players can deliver.
positioningChoices.multiCompetences: Three to five areas you master, each backed by solid client references.
positioningChoices.generaliste: You answer a wide range of needs, without limiting yourself to one specialty.
positioningChoices.regiePure: Staff augmentation: personnel delegation billed per day. You place profiles with the client, who directs the work; you don't commit to an outcome.
positioningChoices.conseilDelivery: You scope the need and then deliver it yourself, with an outcome commitment (fixed price) rather than just time spent.

staffingModel.label: How do you work with your consultants?

targetSectors.label: Which sectors do you target?
targetSectors.subtitle: Several choices allowed — the sectors where you want to find accounts

targetCompanyTypes.label: Which company formats do you want to address?
targetCompanyTypes.subtitle: Multiple choices allowed — it calibrates the account size {{brand}} prioritizes for you

geoZones.label: What's your main geographic area?
geoZones.subtitle: Multiple choices allowed — it prioritizes your searches, never hides any
geoZones.rationale: It never filters anything silently: beyond your area, we automatically widen to all of France instead of hiding accounts from you.

remoteAndTravelScope.label: Remote work and travel — under what conditions?
remoteAndTravelScope.subtitle: Multiple choices allowed — distinct from your geographic area, it says under what conditions you take assignments

zoneCapabilityStatus.label: On your target zones, where do you stand?
zoneCapabilityStatus.subtitle: Multiple choices allowed — distinguishes a proven capability from an intent, never conflated

mainSalesPain.label: What's your biggest sales challenge today?
mainSalesPain.rationale: We use it to pick the action plan and modules we show you first — never to grade you.

recruitsForClients.label: Do you also do recruitment — placing someone on a permanent contract at your client?
recruitsForClients.subtitle: If so, an account’s job postings are no longer filtered to IT roles: every opening becomes a lead.

options.yes: Yes, I also place people on permanent contracts at my clients
options.no: No, I do not place permanent profiles
options.services_only: No, services only (time & materials, fixed price)
options.to_develop: It is an activity I want to develop

workspaceProfile.label: How do you work with your clients?
workspaceProfile.subtitle: On fixed-price work, navigation centres on projects to scope and follow; staffing moves to the background. Change it in Settings.

options.staffing: I place consultants at my clients (time and materials, staffing)
options.forfait_conseil: I scope and follow fixed-price projects delivered by the client’s own teams

idealClientSize.label: What size is your ideal client?
idealClientSize.subtitle: Distinct from the company type, in the next question

idealClientStructure.label: What structure is your ideal client?
idealClientStructure.subtitle: A group, a subsidiary, an SME or the public sector: the way in is not the same.

idealClientMaturity.label: What maturity is your ideal client?
idealClientMaturity.subtitle: The client's stage of life, not yours — select everything that fits.

idealClientTerritory.label: Where is your ideal client located?
idealClientTerritory.rationale: Distinct from your own hunting zone: this asks about the CLIENT's location.
idealClientTerritory.subtitle: The CLIENT's location, distinct from your own hunting zone.

idealClientAccessibility.label: How accessible is this client today?

idealClientMaxSalesCycle.label: What sales cycle are you willing to accept?
idealClientMaxSalesCycle.subtitle: The cycle you can TOLERATE, not necessarily the one you observe today

idealClientMinDealSize.label: What's the minimum deal size you accept?

idealClientReferencementConstraints.label: What supplier-listing constraints do you face with this client?
idealClientReferencementConstraints.subtitle: What you must clear before you can invoice: supplier listing, framework agreement, audit.

idealClientCurrentState.label: Where do you already stand with this client profile?
idealClientCurrentState.subtitle: Check everything that applies — several can apply at once

realResponseLevel.label: At what level do you actually get responses?
realResponseLevel.subtitle: Not the one you target, the one you actually get

accessOrienteur.label: Who can guide you internally once the first contact is made?

entryChannelsDependency.label: Which channel(s) do you depend on most?
entryChannelsDependency.subtitle: The one(s) without which your pipeline would stop

entryChannelsPrerequisites.label: What prerequisites limit access to a channel?
entryChannelsPrerequisites.subtitle: Accreditation, minimum budget, existing relationship...

entryChannelsSaturation.label: On which channel(s) have you hit a limit?
entryChannelsSaturation.subtitle: Time, volume, available contacts — a limit already reached

serviceTypes.label: What types of service do you offer?
serviceTypes.subtitle: Beyond your general positioning: staffing, fixed-price, consulting, audit… select everything you actually bill for.

serviceTypesProven.label: Which have you already sold?
serviceTypesProven.subtitle: The services you have a real mission or reference for — not a theoretical capability.

serviceTypesDesired.label: Which do you want to develop?
serviceTypesDesired.subtitle: Not offered yet today: it stays an ambition, never a proof.

serviceTypesChoices.regie: Personnel delegation billed per day: the client directs the day-to-day work, your consultant can work on-site or remotely.
serviceTypesChoices.forfait: A scope and a price fixed in advance: you commit to a deliverable, not to time billed.
serviceTypesChoices.conseil: You bring expertise and recommendations, without necessarily delivering what follows yourself.
serviceTypesChoices.audit: You assess an existing situation and hand back a written diagnosis, without running the action that follows.
serviceTypesChoices.centreDeServices: A dedicated team continuously handles the client's requests, with service commitments tracked over time.
serviceTypesChoices.assistanceTechnique: A consultant placed at the client's disposal, billed on time spent, under the client's technical direction.
serviceTypesChoices.sousTraitance: You work on behalf of another provider, who remains the end client's only direct point of contact.
serviceTypesChoices.sousTraitanceRang2: You work on behalf of a subcontractor, one step further removed from the end client.
serviceTypesChoices.produitOuFormation: You sell a product or a training course, rather than bespoke service time.
serviceTypesChoices.servicesManages: You run and support a scope for the client over time, against agreed service levels.
serviceTypesChoices.produitSolutionEditee: You sell or integrate a solution you publish yourself, with its licence or subscription.
serviceTypesChoices.recrutementPermanent: You place permanent hires with the client without employing them yourself.
serviceTypesChoices.bureauEtudes: You take on an engineering study or project, from scoping to the delivered file.

userRoleChoices.founderCeo: Decides commercial strategy and signs the most strategic accounts.
userRoleChoices.directeurCommercial: Leads the sales team and the whole company's revenue.
userRoleChoices.headOfSales: Runs the sales team day to day: targets, pipeline, coaching.
userRoleChoices.businessManager: Carries both mission sales and following up placed consultants.
userRoleChoices.accountManager: Grows and retains a portfolio of accounts already signed.
userRoleChoices.businessDeveloper: Hunts and signs new accounts, without managing an existing portfolio.
userRoleChoices.sdrBdr: Qualifies prospects and books meetings, without closing the sale itself.
userRoleChoices.talentManagerRecruteur: Finds and screens consultants — a recruiting title, not a sales one.
userRoleChoices.consultantIngenieurAffaires: Runs missions AND grows their own client portfolio.
userRoleChoices.directeurDeBu: Runs an autonomous business unit inside a larger group.
userRoleChoices.directeurAgence: Runs a local agency, sales and delivery included.
userRoleChoices.responsableStaffing: Decides who goes on which mission — staffing and bench, not selling.
userRoleChoices.advFinance: Tracks mission billing and collections, without selling them.
userRoleChoices.freelanceActiviteIndividuelle: Sells and delivers alone, for their own account — no structure around them.
userRoleChoices.operationsCommerciales: Runs sales process, tooling and data — no account book of their own.
userRoleChoices.purCommercial: Focused on selling, never involved in delivering the missions.
userRoleChoices.commercialCultureTechnique: Sells with a real grasp of delivery, without delivering it themselves.
userRoleChoices.hybrideBusinessDelivery: Genuinely splits their time between selling and missions.
userRoleChoices.ancienConsultantDevenuCommercial: Sells on the strength of recent hands-on delivery experience.
userRoleChoices.purTechniqueDelivery: Focused on missions, with no direct sales activity.
userRoleChoices.recrutementTalent: Describes how you work, not your title: recruiting comes before selling.
userRoleChoices.directionManagement: Describes how you work: you lead the team, without selling yourself day to day.
userRoleChoices.responsableAdv: You run sales administration: orders, contracts, invoicing and payment follow-up.
userRoleChoices.responsableDelivery: You steer how missions are carried out at clients and the quality of what is delivered.
userRoleChoices.responsableAchatsPartenariats: You manage purchasing, subcontracting and the partners who bring you deals or profiles.
userRoleChoices.responsableMarketing: You own the brand, content and campaigns that generate sales conversations.
userRoleChoices.responsableBureauEtudes: You lead an engineering design office: you scope, price and deliver engineering studies.

caseStudyResults.label: Do you have concrete results to show?
caseStudyResults.subtitle: One result, numeric or qualitative, per mission or client, in a few words.

clientTestimonials.label: Do you have client testimonials to cite?
clientTestimonials.subtitle: A quote or a contact who can vouch for your work.
clientTestimonials.placeholder: E.g.: “A responsive, autonomous team” — CIO, client X

referenceAccounts.label: Which companies can you cite as references?
referenceAccounts.subtitle: The company name alone, no detail — useful for talking about comparable accounts.

expertiseNoConcreteProof.label: Which expertises have no concrete proof yet?
expertiseNoConcreteProof.subtitle: No client reference, mission, or testimonial — just an intent to develop it for now.

expertiseClientReference.label: Which expertises have a client reference to show?
expertiseClientReference.subtitle: Select the ones where a real client already backs up what you claim.

expertisePersonalExperience.label: Which expertises rest on your personal experience?
expertisePersonalExperience.subtitle: Select the ones you master through your own background, beyond any client reference.

expertisePartner.label: Which expertises rest on a partner?
expertisePartner.subtitle: Select the ones where a partner carries part of what you offer.

expertiseTalentPool.label: Which expertises have an available pool of consultants?
expertiseTalentPool.subtitle: Select the ones where consultants are ready to be staffed right now.

staffingModes.label: Which modes do you actually use, beyond your main one?
staffingModes.subtitle: Select everything you actually combine — recruit-on-demand, subcontracting, nearshore, partners.

profileValidationMethods.label: How do you validate a profile before proposing it?
profileValidationMethods.subtitle: Select everything that applies.

contractualConstraints.label: What contractual constraints apply to your missions?
contractualConstraints.subtitle: What binds you once the assignment is signed — select everything that applies.

decisionsAlone.label: Which decisions do you make alone, without having to ask?
decisionsAlone.subtitle: Select everything that applies — this shapes what {{copilot}} proposes to you, never what you're allowed to do.

decisionsToValidate.label: Which decisions do you have to get validated by someone else?
decisionsToValidate.subtitle: Select everything that applies — a decision can appear here and in the previous question.

peopleManaged.label: Who do you manage?
peopleManaged.subtitle: By function, never by name — select everything that applies.

recruitmentAccountsAuthority.label: Recruiting a new client account: is that your call?
recruitmentAccountsAuthority.subtitle: Your answer shapes what {{copilot}} proposes to you, never what you're authorized to do.

staffingAuthority.label: Deciding a staffing move: is that your call?
staffingAuthority.subtitle: Your answer shapes what {{copilot}} proposes to you, never what you're authorized to do.

marginBillingAuthority.label: Margin and billing: is that your call?
marginBillingAuthority.subtitle: Your answer shapes what {{copilot}} proposes to you, never what you're authorized to do.

toolsAccess.label: Which tools do you have access to?
toolsAccess.subtitle: Select everything that applies.

inviteAuthority.label: Inviting someone into the workspace: is that your call?
inviteAuthority.subtitle: Your answer shapes what {{copilot}} proposes to you, never what you're authorized to do — the actual invite stays a workspace right.

associatesCount.label: How many partners does the company have?
associatesCount.subtitle: As in owners/shareholders, not total headcount.

recruitersTeamSize.label: How many recruiters work on the talent pool?
recruitersTeamSize.subtitle: A band is enough.

deliveryTeamSize.label: How many people in delivery (missions, management, bench)?
deliveryTeamSize.subtitle: The whole delivery function, not just consultants currently on a mission.

marketingTeamSize.label: How many people dedicated to marketing?
marketingTeamSize.subtitle: Part-time or full-time, a band is enough.

opsTeamSize.label: How many people dedicated to operations (admin, billing, internal HR…)?
opsTeamSize.subtitle: A band is enough.

teamCoordinationMode.label: How does the team coordinate day to day?
teamCoordinationMode.subtitle: Whichever best describes how you actually work.

prioritySectors.label: Among those sectors, which ones are genuinely priorities this year?
prioritySectors.subtitle: Two is a choice. Beyond that we'll ask again — without ever stopping you from moving on.

referenceSectors.label: In which of these sectors do you have a real reference?
referenceSectors.subtitle: An ongoing or past mission — not just a targeted sector.

weeklySalesTimeDeclared.label: How much time a week do you say you give to business development?
weeklySalesTimeDeclared.subtitle: The time you ANNOUNCE, the one you would quote in a meeting

weeklySalesTimeProtected.label: Of that time, how much actually holds in an ordinary week?
weeklySalesTimeProtected.subtitle: Not what you aim for: what survives a normal week

weeklySalesTimeResidual.label: And once everything else has been served, how much is left?
weeklySalesTimeResidual.subtitle: We do not work it out for you: subtracting two bands would invent a number you never gave

competingWorkloads.label: What takes the rest of your week?
competingWorkloads.subtitle: Several answers possible

workloadVariability.label: Is your workload the same from one week to the next?

weeklySalesTimeSlots.label: When does your commercial time actually land?
weeklySalesTimeSlots.subtitle: Several answers possible

protectedSlotCapacity.label: Can you block a slot and keep it?

dossierContinuityPractices.label: What holds on your accounts today, even when you are away?
dossierContinuityPractices.subtitle: Several answers possible. This is what keeps an account from starting over

dossierContinuityBreaks.label: Where do your accounts most often fall through?
dossierContinuityBreaks.subtitle: Several answers possible

entryChannelsUsed.label: Which channels does your business actually come in through?
entryChannelsUsed.subtitle: Tick what you really use. A channel you don't use isn't a failed channel, it is simply absent.

entryChannelsPeriod.label: For which of these channels do you know the time window your numbers cover?
entryChannelsPeriod.subtitle: A volume without a time window attached is a rough order of magnitude, not a measurement.

entryChannelsMeasured.label: For which of these channels do you know the numbers?
entryChannelsMeasured.subtitle: Volume, replies, meetings, starts. Anything you don't measure stays written "not measured", never counted as zero.

entryChannelsLastStarts.label: Which channels produced your most recent mission starts?
entryChannelsLastStarts.subtitle: Three at most. What gets seen and what actually lands are two different things, and we never mix them.

entryChannelsTimeSplit.label: Where does most of your sales time go?
entryChannelsTimeSplit.subtitle: Two channels at most. This is your real week, not your intention.

formerClientsCountBand.label: Former clients: roughly how many?
formerClientsCountBand.subtitle: A band is enough — nobody knows their exact count to the client.

formerColleaguesCountBand.label: Former colleagues: roughly how many could speak for you?
formerColleaguesCountBand.subtitle: A network of peers, not clients — same rough-band principle.

partnersCountBand.label: Partners and second-tier firms: roughly how many do you know personally?
partnersCountBand.subtitle: Not the number of partner companies: the number of people you can reach out to directly.

referrersCountBand.label: People who could refer you: roughly how many?
referrersCountBand.subtitle: Those who could put you in touch, not the referrals already received.

warmRelationsCountBand.label: Warm relationships: roughly how many, across all channels?
warmRelationsCountBand.subtitle: It doesn't matter where they came from — former clients, colleagues, partners, or elsewhere.

activityMeasuresTracked.label: What do you actually count today?
activityMeasuresTracked.subtitle: Each step has its own unit: accounts, contacts, meetings, starts. They never add up together.

activityReferencePeriod.label: What period do these numbers cover?
activityReferencePeriod.subtitle: Without a period, a number is only an order of magnitude, and no rate can be computed from it.

toolingCrm.label: Your CRM — who uses it?
toolingCrm.subtitle: The tool where your accounts, contacts and opportunities live

toolingAts.label: Your ATS — who uses it?
toolingAts.subtitle: Where applications, profiles and skill dossiers live

toolingErp.label: Your ERP — who uses it?
toolingErp.subtitle: Where assignments, staffing and invoicing live

toolingMailbox.label: Your mailbox — who uses it?
toolingMailbox.subtitle: We only locate where your exchanges live: answering here opens no access to your inbox

toolingCalendar.label: Your calendar — who uses it?
toolingCalendar.subtitle: Where your meetings and availability live

toolingDrive.label: Your shared file space — who uses it?
toolingDrive.subtitle: Where your proposals, contracts and sales documents live

toolingInternalNames.label: A home-grown tool? Give it its name
toolingInternalNames.subtitle: Your CRM, ATS or ERP was built in-house: name it, one at a time

toolingSpreadsheet.label: Your spreadsheets — who uses them?
toolingSpreadsheet.subtitle: The account lists and trackers rebuilt by hand every week

toolingEnrichment.label: A tool to find contact details — who uses it?
toolingEnrichment.subtitle: What you use to find an email or a phone number when you don't have them

toolingSourcingPlatform.label: The platforms where you receive or post needs — who uses them?
toolingSourcingPlatform.subtitle: Tender portals, marketplaces, your clients' supplier spaces

toolingBi.label: Your reporting and steering tool — who uses it?
toolingBi.subtitle: Where you look at your numbers, when they aren't already in another tool

toolingPersonalNotes.label: Your personal notes — who can see them?
toolingPersonalNotes.subtitle: What you write during a call and nobody else sees

toolingReference.label: Where do your sales data really live today?
toolingReference.subtitle: The source you reopen when you need to be sure — the next questions are about it

toolingReferenceConfidence.label: How much do you trust it?
toolingReferenceConfidence.subtitle: Your own reading, not a grade: nothing is computed from this answer

toolingReferenceExport.label: Can you get your data out of it?

toolingDuplicates.label: Does the same information live in several places?
toolingDuplicates.subtitle: We'll suggest matches — nothing is ever merged without you

toolingPain.label: What costs you the most time in this chain?
toolingPain.subtitle: One sentence, in your own words
toolingPain.placeholder: E.g. I re-enter the same contacts in three places

salesFreins.label: What is really stopping you from moving forward?
salesFreins.subtitle: Several choices allowed, the ones that really weigh — if yours isn't listed, write it

freinAttempted.label: What have you already tried to lift that blocker?
freinAttempted.subtitle: Even if it didn't work — especially if it didn't work
freinAttempted.placeholder: E.g. a calling session every Monday morning

freinStopped.label: What stopped?
freinStopped.placeholder: E.g. I kept it up for three weeks, then nothing

freinStoppedReason.label: Why?
freinStoppedReason.subtitle: That answer is what tells a symptom apart from a real bottleneck
freinStoppedReason.placeholder: E.g. Monday mornings are taken by staffing reviews

heardAboutBellum.label: How did you hear about {{brand}}?
heardAboutBellum.subtitle: Optional — only used to know how sales reps find us, never to assess your profile. You can skip this question.

companyLocations.label: Where is your company based?
companyLocations.subtitle: Your HQ, then your offices. Pick from the catalog, or add one you can't find. Distinct from your prospecting zones, asked later.

uncoveredActivityNote.label: Is there anything important about your business that my questions didn't cover?
uncoveredActivityNote.subtitle: E.g.: internal constraint, new market, key client, partner, territory conflict, offer in progress, personal goal, side project.
uncoveredActivityNote.placeholder: Write freely — {{copilot}} reads it and proposes facts to review, without confirming anything on your behalf

activityNature.label: How would you describe your activity?
activityNature.subtitle: Several activities can coexist. None imposes a client sector or a technology.

dataSources.label: Which useful data will you be able to reuse?
dataSources.subtitle: Reuse will depend on access, scope and actual rights.

tools.label: Which tools do you already use?
tools.subtitle: This choice describes your equipment. It connects no tool and does not certify that an integration is available.

workflowPain.label: Which manual task would you like to stop redoing?
workflowPain.subtitle: Describe the starting point and the expected result, rather than a feature name.

deliveryFrictions.label: Which mission or sales-admin topics do you want to follow more closely?
deliveryFrictions.subtitle: A document awaited, an invoice and a payment remain different states.

firstName.label: What would you like {{copilot}} to call you?
firstName.subtitle: The first name personalises the tone; it changes neither your sign-in identity nor your rights.

scopeLevel.label: Which scope do you answer for?
scopeLevel.subtitle: Headcounts and goals must concern this same scope. This statement gives no access to other teams' data.

scopeUnit.label: What is the name of this agency, BU or scope?
scopeUnit.subtitle: Optional. Does not replace the company name.

autonomy.label: Which way of working do you want with {{copilot}}?
autonomy.subtitle: A preference is not a permission to send. Mandates, permissions and budgets are configured separately.

contextPolicy.label: How would you like to start in {{copilot}}?
contextPolicy.subtitle: Neutral does not erase what you give in a request. A new Discover search stays without implicit preselection.

offerPitch.label: What sets you apart, concretely?
offerPitch.subtitle: Explain the problem you handle and how you intervene, no mandatory slogan.

languageCapabilities.label: Which languages can you work in?
languageCapabilities.subtitle: Capability statement, to be confirmed for each profile and each mission.

priorityExpertise.label: Which expertise do you want to put forward now?
priorityExpertise.subtitle: Optional. They give a priority order; all your expertise is kept.

skillTechnos.label: Which tools, methods or know-how refine your offer?
skillTechnos.subtitle: Add your own terms: SQL, CATIA, Lean, IFRS, pharmacovigilance… A suggestion is never an assumed skill.

benchStatus.label: Do you have profiles to position soon?
benchStatus.subtitle: Actual availability will be checked for each person.

recruitingPriorities.label: Which recruiting or staffing challenge do you want to address?
recruitingPriorities.subtitle: Several choices allowed.

commercialLimits.label: Which economic benchmarks must be preserved?
commercialLimits.subtitle: Optional: purchase budget, selling price, target margin and currency. Do not confuse cost and client rate.

currency.label: Which currency do you express your economic benchmarks in?
currency.subtitle: No exchange rate or automatic conversion is applied in this preview.

targetNature.label: Do you want to work with end clients, partners, or both?
targetNature.subtitle: A partner target remains distinct from an end client.

targetSize.label: Which company sizes do you want to explore?
targetSize.subtitle: These categories serve scoping, with no assumed regulatory threshold.

countryScope.label: Which countries can you really work in?
countryScope.subtitle: Separate operational countries from zones merely considered.

geographyDetail.label: Which precise geographic scope should be kept?
geographyDetail.subtitle: City, radius, sites or countries: say what matters. A presence does not guarantee that a purchase decision is made on site.

noGo.label: Which exclusions or constraints must we respect?
noGo.subtitle: For example: no tier 2, accounts not to be approached, limited travel. Enter no secret or unnecessary personal data.

accountAccess.label: Which accounts do you already have a relationship or access with?
accountAccess.subtitle: Specify the nature of the access: relationship, past mission, framework agreement… An account in the CRM is not a procurement listing.

horizon.label: Over what horizon are you looking for a first result?
horizon.subtitle: This horizon helps choose an entry route, not promise a signature.

successTarget.label: Which concrete result would tell you {{brand}} is useful?
successTarget.subtitle: Example: identify three accounts and prepare the right contacts; or unblock pending invoices.

tour.dialogDescription: A guided tour of {{brand}}'s key screens, one at a time.
tour.subtitle: {{brand}} in {{total}} screens, at your own pace.

dashboard.promise: Your starting point every morning: what's waiting for you today, and where your portfolio stands.
does: Work through your setup step by step, until your workspace is ready to use.
Read your personal numbers — portfolio, follow-ups due, overdue items, messages from the last seven days — and click one to go straight to the work it points at.
Ask {{copilot}} what she would make of your day, without leaving the screen.

search.promise: The founding gesture: you type a company's name, and {{brand}} turns it into a full account brief.
does: Lock the exact registry entity — the right registration number, not its namesake.
Choose the scope analysed: the whole group, the country, subsidiaries, or a scope you compose yourself.
See the announced cost and confirm: nothing is collected or charged until you have confirmed.

accounts.promise: Every analysis becomes a dossier here — a broken-down score, the dominant signal of the moment, the next action.
does: Sort your portfolio by sales stage: to triage, watching, promising, client, deprioritised.
Switch lens to read the same accounts differently — through invoicing, or through this week's priorities.
Open an account for its org chart, its action plan and ready-to-send messages.

contacts.promise: The people {{brand}} found at your accounts, and the best way in for each of them.
does: Filter by role, by company or by reachable channel — and isolate your dormant network at six, twelve or twenty-four months.
Enrich several contacts at once, each detail carrying the date it was verified.
Spot someone who has changed employer: {{brand}} flags it rather than letting you write to the wrong person.

targets.promise: The lists you prepare for a session, a campaign or a period — each one referencing its accounts and contacts without copying them.
does: Create a list with its objective, then add accounts or contacts already in your workspace.
Set a priority, an owner and a work status for each record in the list.
Note the next action for each target, until it is contacted or dropped.

actions.promise: What is waiting for a move from you, account by account — and the trace of everything already done.
does: Review the action centre: to approve, scheduled, in progress, done, to resume.
Approve or dismiss yourself a write prepared for your CRM, before it leaves.
Find the activity log again, filtered by type, status, period, account or team member.

chat.promise: {{copilot}}, your copilot: she answers with what {{brand}} already knows about your accounts, contacts and assignments.
does: Ask her about your whole portfolio, or frame the conversation on a single account.
Pin a fact so she keeps it in mind from one conversation to the next.
Read her answers with their source and its date, and approve yourself what she prepares — she never sends anything on her own.

consultants.promise: Who you can put forward, and on what terms: the skills, rate and real availability of your talent pool.
does: Add a profile by dropping their CV, then filter by skill, rate, area, language or seniority.
Read the availability derived from assignments, shown next to the declared one when the two disagree.
See the skills you are missing — those for which you have already turned down several needs.

projects.promise: What your clients are looking for, from detection to signature: the project pipeline and the needs that come out of it.
does: Switch between the pipeline and your portfolio, as a kanban or as a table.
Move a project between stages — and name the reason when it is lost, so the next time benefits from it.
Isolate projects with no next action: the ones going quiet without anyone noticing.

missions.promise: What is signed and what it produces: staffing, deadlines, risks, and what is ready to invoice.
does: Read your assignments from three angles: running, renewals, ready to invoice.
Spot at a glance the ones up for renewal, the ones with no end date, the ones carrying a risk.
Choose your columns — margin, stage age, contract type, next action.

pilotage.promise: Your activity from above: the links of the sales chain, where it jams, and what changed once you acted.
does: Read each link with its alert threshold, and the sentence saying how many cases it was computed on.
Open the decision cards: the few moves genuinely waiting — and nothing at all when nothing is waiting.
Consult the indicator dictionary to know exactly what each number counts.

integrations.promise: Plug your own tools into {{brand}}: what you already do elsewhere should not be typed in twice.
does: Connect your CRM, your mailbox and calendar, your team channels, your ATS or ERP, your phone system.
See the real state of each connection: operational, read-only, authorisation expired, no recent activity.
Follow “where to start”, which disappears on its own once it has nothing left to recommend.

role_functions_practiced.subtitle: A job title doesn't say everything. {{brand}} relies on what you really do, not on what your role description says.

role_tenure.label: How long have you been in this role?
role_tenure.subtitle: Calibrates support: more method early on, more execution later.

industry_tenure.label: How long have you worked in consulting / IT services?
industry_tenure.subtitle: Tells a newcomer from an expert — the wording of recommendations follows.

individual_goal.label: What is your main individual goal?
individual_goal.subtitle: Daily recommendations will point at THIS goal.

monthly_target.label: What is your 30-day target?
monthly_target.subtitle: Gives {{copilot}} a concrete number: she can tell whether you are ahead or behind.

company_age.subtitle: A young firm and an established one don't open accounts the same way.

company_size.label: How big is your company?
company_size.subtitle: Shapes the access strategy: framework agreements, subcontracting or direct approach.

company_group_structure.label: Is your company independent, a parent company, or a subsidiary?
company_group_structure.subtitle: A number of branch offices doesn't say who owns whom — tell us yourself.

consultants_on_mission.label: How many consultants do you actually have on assignment?
consultants_on_mission.subtitle: Measures real delivery capacity — not the one on the website.

consultants_in_pipe.label: How many consultants / profiles are in your active bench?
consultants_in_pipe.subtitle: With no bench, {{brand}} prioritises opening accounts over pushing profiles.

team_overlap.label: Do colleagues work on the same accounts, sectors or territories?
team_overlap.subtitle: Lets us flag duplicates before two reps trip over each other.

ramp_up_capacity.label: How fast can you start?
ramp_up_capacity.subtitle: A client's urgency only matters if you can meet the deadline.

avg_deal_size.label: What is your average deal / assignment size?
avg_deal_size.subtitle: Filters out off-calibre accounts instead of suggesting them.

target_margin.label: What margin do you target?
target_margin.subtitle: This lets {{brand}} recommend the right number of active deals, so volume is never mistaken for profitability.

portfolio_size.label: How many accounts are currently in your portfolio?
portfolio_size.subtitle: Calibrates load: we won't push 20 new accounts at someone already carrying 80.

accounts_relationship_status.label: What is the status of most of your accounts?
accounts_relationship_status.subtitle: Changes the action plan entirely: open, revive or grow.

go_to_market_channels.label: Do you work direct or through partners?
go_to_market_channels.subtitle: Determines the entry points {{brand}} suggests.

public_sector_practice.label: Where do you stand on public procurement?
public_sector_practice.subtitle: Framework, lot-based bidding or subcontracting: three very different ways in.

growth_target_zones.label: Which areas do you want to grow into?
growth_target_zones.subtitle: The ones you're aiming for, not the ones you already cover — {{brand}} never reads them as a capability.

regulated_sector_readiness.label: What can you show a bank or an insurer?
regulated_sector_readiness.subtitle: These accounts screen on compliance and references before any tech talk.

partner_relationship.label: What is your relationship with your current partners?
partner_relationship.subtitle: Tier-2 work hinges on collaboration history as much as on price.

partners_regular_count.label: How many regular partners (IT services firms, consultancies, tier-1 primes) do you really work with today?
partners_regular_count.subtitle: The ones business regularly flows through, with a contract in place. {{brand}} turns them into your partner workload — never guessing the number.

partners_occasional_count.label: And how many occasional partners?
partners_occasional_count.subtitle: The ones you call on when needed. They stay outside your active workload: {{brand}} names them, it never adds them to the regular ones.

weekly_calls.label: How many calls do you make per week?
weekly_calls.subtitle: Used to propose a realistic cadence, not a theoretical routine.

weekly_emails.label: How many prospecting emails do you send per week?
weekly_emails.subtitle: Same rule: suggested actions must fit your real week.

weekly_linkedin.label: How many LinkedIn touches do you make per week?
